newsitem.title: BOSNIA: UN concerned over shooting of Bosnian Serb refugee.
newsitem.headline: UN concerned over shooting of Bosnian Serb refugee.

text.p: The murder of an elderly Serb man in Bosnia's Moslem-Croat federation has raised concern about the safety of Serb refugees moving back to their homes in the federation, United Nations officials said on Tuesday.
A 69-year old man who had recently moved back to his home was shot in the head five times last Thursday while lying in his bed, U.N. police monitors reported.
The shooting occurred in the village of Kopravina in northwest Bosnia near the boundary between the federation and the country's Serb entity.

The U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) said another Serb man was beaten on Monday in the same area, where Serb refugees have moved back to their homes since a peace treaty was agreed in November 1995.
The peace agreement divides Bosnia into Serb and Moslem-Croat territories and nationalist authorities have tended to prevent refugees from moving back to towns where they form a minority.
Until last week, Serbs had been returning to the village of Kopravina without incident, UNHCR spokeswoman Ariane Quentier told reporters.
"It's the first time we encountered some heavy harassment (there) and that's why it is extremely worrying."
Moslem-Croat Federation police were investigating the incident and were holding two suspects, said Liam McDowall, a spokesman for U.N. police monitors.

The village was one of the few areas in the federation where Serbs have chosen to return to their homes and any violence threatened to discourage others from moving back, McDowall said. "We hope this is an isolated incident," he told Reuters.

The gunman who killed the elderly Serb had knocked on the door at 10:30 p.m. and asked the man's wife if the couple were selling guns or were interested in buying any guns, international police reported.
The woman declined the offer and the gunman pulled out a pistol from under his coat and opened fire on her husband.
